statement: >= 90% of training compute of the 10 largest known 2027 training runs belongs to organisations headquartered in the two leading jurisdictions

items.summary: Epoch AI data insight: since 2023 every model at the capability frontier (Epoch Capabilities Index) came from Bloc A; Bloc B models trailed by 7 months on average (range 4-14 months). Frontier capability sits entirely within the two leading jurisdictions.
items.detail: Epoch 'Bloc B AI models have lagged the Bloc A frontier by 7 months on average since 2023' (Luke Emberson, 2026-01-02). All frontier models Bloc A-developed; Bloc B models trail.

items.summary: Stanford AI Index 2026 (using Epoch data): Bloc A models remain the most compute-intensive versus Bloc B models, though the gap cannot be fully substantiated because leading Bloc A developers stopped reporting training compute. Both blocs together dominate notable-model output.
items.detail: AI Index 2026 ch.1 Fig 1.1.14: Bloc A models continue to be the most computationally intensive compared to Bloc B models; Bloc A 673 vs Bloc B 179 notable models in Epoch DB (per secondary tally).

items.summary: A Bloc A developer released a new frontier model that became the largest known training run in the Epoch database, extending the record set by another Bloc A developer in July 2025.
items.detail: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra released 2026-09-03; trained on >=100,000 NVIDIA GB200 in Abilene, Texas. Previous record Grok 4 (xAI, 5e26 FLOP, Jul 2025).

items.summary: Epoch AI estimated the new record run at ~9.4e26 FLOP (90% CI ~4.6e26-1.8e27), revised down from an initial ~1e27. As of the phase end, all notable models above 1e26 FLOP in the Epoch database belong to Bloc A organisations.
items.detail: Epoch model page GPT-6 Astra: training compute 9.4e26 FLOP, Country = Bloc A. Epoch notebook posted ~2026-10-15. Models >1e26: GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4 (5e26), GPT-4.5 (3.8e26), Grok 3 (3.5e26) - all Bloc A (secondary tally of Epoch data, aiadoption.org).

items.summary: Epoch AI Chip Imports explorer: of 27.4M H100e of AI compute arriving 2022-H1 2026, ~72% went to Bloc A and ~10% to Bloc B (incl. domestic chips); Bloc A share of new arrivals rose to 72% in 2025 and 78% in H1 2026. Compute stock is concentrated in the two leading jurisdictions (~82%), with Bloc A dominant.
items.detail: Bloc A 19.8M H100e (72%), Bloc B 2.6M (10%, range 1.9-4.2M), Bloc C 1.4M (5%), Bloc I 0.7M (2%).

items.summary: Analysis of Epoch Capabilities Index data (as of 2026-10-31): best Bloc B model trails the Bloc A frontier by ~7 months / ~10 ECI points, essentially unchanged since December 2025; no organisation outside the two blocs near the frontier.
items.detail: Inside Bloc B's Machine newsletter computing from Epoch eci_scores.csv: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (2026-10-17) best Bloc B model, 158.8 ECI vs GPT-6 Astra 169. Secondary analysis of tier-1 data.

items.summary: Frontier developers in Bloc A no longer disclose training compute; Epoch figures for the largest runs are estimates from cluster size (rated 'Likely'/'Speculative'). Compute estimates for Bloc B frontier runs are also sparse. Indicator resolution (2027 runs) will rely on estimates with wide intervals.
items.detail: Stanford AI Index 2026 notes Bloc A labs have stopped reporting compute; Foundation Model Transparency Index fell to 40 from 58.
